title: C4F - Tree Allometry
text:
Introduction
Define the project.

title: Model
text:
\[\begin{align}
log(agb) \sim \mathcal N (log(\mu), \sigma) \\
\mu = \sum_{i \in p} \gamma_s \times 0.0673 \times [wd_i \times dbh_i^2 \times \frac{\alpha_f \times dbh_i}{\beta_f+dbh_i}]^{0.976} \\
\gamma_s = exp(\epsilon_s \times \sigma_s) \\
\alpha_f \sim \mathcal N (\alpha_0,\sigma_a) \\
\beta_f \sim \mathcal N (\beta_0,\sigma_b) \\
\epsilon_s  \sim \mathcal N (0,1) \\
\end{align}\]
With plot biomass \(agb\) linked to the sum of tree biomass \(\mu\) defined on tree wood density \(wd_i\), tree diameter \(dbh_i\) and tree height \(h_i\) itself derived from \(dbh_i\) following a Michaelis Menten law with parameters \(\alpha_f\) and \(\beta_f\) depending on the factor \(f\) being the intersection of the \(system\) and the \(origin\) and a random parameters \(\gamma_s\) representing species random effect.

Modelling remark

The model is working better when modelling total AGB and not per hectare AGB that works better when computed posthoc (beware also the division by 1000 for units). It seems also really important to keep low AGB plots for tree height scaling parameters (AGB<10t/ha).
I developed a version pre-computing log agb and mainly using a cumulative sum trick to reduce computing time (but parrallelisation is useless).




Code
trees <- read_csv2("data/all_tree_corr.csv") %>% 
  select(-1) %>% 
  mutate(system = gsub("_", " ", system)) %>% 
  select(database, id_plot, id_tree, system, origin, dbh, H, genusCorr, speciesCorr) %>% 
  rename(h = H, genus = genusCorr, species = speciesCorr) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(dbh), !is.na(h))
trees$wd <- BIOMASS::getWoodDensity(genus = trees$genus,
                                    species = trees$species,
                                    stand = trees$id_plot)$meanWD
plots <- trees %>% 
  mutate(agb = 0.0673*(wd*dbh^2*h)^0.976) %>% 
  group_by(database, system, id_plot) %>% 
  summarise(agb = sum(agb)) %>% 
  left_join(select(read_csv2("data/all_plot_corr.csv"), 
                   id_plot, area_plot.ha)) %>% 
  mutate(agb_ha = agb/10^3/area_plot.ha) %>% 
  filter(agb_ha > 0, agb_ha < 1000) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(plotnum = as.numeric(as.factor(id_plot)))
trees <- trees %>% 
  left_join(plots) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(plotnum)) %>% 
  select(-agb, -agb_ha, -area_plot.ha) %>% 
  mutate(factornum = as.numeric(as.factor(paste(system, origin)))) %>% 
  mutate(speciesnum = as.numeric(as.factor(paste(genus, species)))) %>% 
  arrange(plotnum, speciesnum, factornum) %>% 
  mutate(obs = 1:n())
positions <- trees %>% 
  group_by(plotnum) %>% 
  summarise(start = min(obs), end = max(obs))
mdata <- list(
  N = nrow(trees),
  P = nrow(plots),
  S = max(trees$speciesnum),
  "F" = max(trees$factornum),
  plot = trees$plotnum,
  species = trees$speciesnum,
  factor = trees$factornum,
  agb = plots$agb,
  agb_ha = plots$agb_ha,
  area = plots$area_plot.ha,
  dbh = trees$dbh,
  wd = trees$wd,
  start = positions$start,
  end = positions$end,
  grainsize = 1
)

  unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(path)
fit <- model$sample(
  data = mdata,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  save_warmup = FALSE,
  output_dir = path,
  refresh = 100
)

              "sigma", "sigma_s", "sigma_a", "sigma_b")) %>%

Code
fit$summary(c("alpha_f", "beta_f"), 
            quantiles = ~ posterior::quantile2(., probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 
                                                            0.5, 0.75, 0.95))) %>% 
  separate(variable, c("parameter", "f", "factornum"), convert = TRUE) %>% 
  select(-f) %>% 
  left_join(select(trees, system, origin, factornum) %>% unique()) %>% 
  select(-factornum) %>% 
  gather(quantile, value, -parameter, -system, -origin) %>% 
  mutate(system = gsub("_", " ", system)) %>% 
  mutate(metric = paste0(parameter, "_", quantile)) %>% 
  select(-parameter, -quantile) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(beta_q50, alpha_q50,
             col = paste0(system, "\n", origin),
             label = paste0(system, "\n", origin))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = beta_q25, xend = beta_q75)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = beta_q5, xend = beta_q95), size = .2) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = alpha_q25, yend = alpha_q75)) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = alpha_q5, yend = alpha_q95), size = .2) +
  geom_point() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(box.padding = 0.4, ) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_discrete(guide = "none") +
  ylab("Asymptotic height [ m ]") +
  xlab("Diameter at 50% height [ cm ]")





Caption.





Some systems are good other seems less, but this is not what the likelihood is optimizing.



Code
coords <- read_csv2("data/all_plot_corr.csv") %>% 
  select(database, id_plot, long, lat)
trees$agb_chave <- BIOMASS::computeAGB(D = trees$dbh, 
                                       WD = trees$wd, 
                                       coord = left_join(trees, coords)[c("long", "lat")])
agb_chave <- trees %>% 
  group_by(database, system, id_plot, plotnum) %>% 
  summarise(chave = sum(agb_chave)) |> 
  left_join(select(read_csv2("data/all_plot_corr.csv"), 
                   id_plot, area_plot.ha)) %>% 
  mutate(chave = chave/area_plot.ha) 
plots %>% 
  left_join(agb_chave) |> 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(model = fit$summary("pred_ha", "median")$median) %>% 
  gather(model, predicted, -database, -system, -id_plot,
         -plotnum, -agb, -agb_ha, -area_plot.ha) %>% 
  rename(observed = agb_ha) %>% 
  mutate(error_log = log(observed) - log(predicted)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(system, error_log, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip()





Caption.





Mixed results about the advantage of the model compared to the ref. Not in the case of the forest. Very important for agroforestry.
Question

Repeat with null model, system only and origin only?
Evaluation? Quality of fit or prediction? Cross-validation?
